title: Dynamical degrees of rational maps
summary: Graphs and topological degrees of dominant rational maps between projective varieties over an arbitrary field; Euler-characteristic intersection numbers; imported nefness (line bundles and the full nef cone of N^1(X/K)) and Kleiman nonnegativity read in these numbers, approximation of nef real classes by ample line bundles, and the positivity package over an arbitrary field (Siu, Hodge inequality on possibly singular surfaces, Khovanskii-Teissier, Siu for products); degrees deg_k(f; L, M) with model independence, positivity, normalization and field-extension invariance, sub-multiplicativity and comparison; dynamical degrees, log-concavity, birational and field-extension invariance, algebraic entropy; projective-space and affine-space examples (forms, morphisms, Cremona, Fibonacci, Frobenius, polynomial maps).

layers.title: Function fields and the graph of a dominant rational map

targets.name: RationalMap.functionFieldPullback / RationalMap.topologicalDegree
targets.statement: For a dominant K-rational map f : X ⤏ Y of varieties over K, f^* : K(Y) -> K(X) is Tau Ceti's Scheme.Hom.functionFieldAlgHom of a K-representative f_V : V -> Y on a dense open V, composed with K(V) = K(X); it is independent of the representative and equals the stalk map induced by RationalMap.fromFunctionField f. e(f) = Module.finrank over f^*K(Y) of K(X). f |-> f^* is a bijection onto K-algebra maps K(Y) -> K(X); (g∘f)^* = f^*∘g^*; e(f) > 0 iff dim X = dim Y (junk 0 otherwise); e(g∘f) = e(f)e(g) in equal dimension; e(f) = 1 iff f^* is an isomorphism iff f is birational (the rational map of a partial isomorphism over K); then Scheme.Birational X Y holds and f^{-1} has pullback (f^*)^{-1}.
hypotheses: X, Y integral, separated, of finite type over K
f dominant and over Spec K
equal dimensions for finiteness and multiplicativity

locator.where: Definition 52.8 (tag 02NY), line 6046; dinhsibony2005 lines 69-70

targets.name: RationalMap.graph
targets.statement: For a K-rational map f : X ⤏ Y of projective varieties, Γ_f is the scheme-theoretic image of (ι_U, f_U) : U -> X ×_K Y, U = f.domain, with projections π_1, π_2. Γ_f is integral, closed, projective, of dimension dim X, independent of the representative; π_1 is a modification with witness U, π_1^{-1}(U) ≅ U; π_2 ∘ γ_f = f_U; f dominant implies π_2 surjective; equal dimensions make π_2 an alteration of generic degree e(f); morphisms give π_1 an isomorphism; birational inverses swap graphs.

f a K-rational map; dominant for the statements on π_2
dim X = dim Y for the alteration statement

targets.name: RationalMap.compositeCorrespondence
targets.statement: For dominant f : X ⤏ Y and g : Y ⤏ Z between projective varieties of the same dimension d, W_{f,g} ⊆ X ×_K Y ×_K Z is the scheme-theoretic image of (ι_U, f_U, (g∘f)_U) : U -> X ×_K Y ×_K Z, U the intersection of the domains of f and g∘f; it uses only the integral source and no integrality of Y ×_K Z (which may be reducible, e.g. P^1_C ×_R P^1_C), so it is not the graph of §1.2 applied to a map into Y ×_K Z. W_{f,g} is an integral projective variety of dimension d, independent of the dense open U; (q_X,q_Y) : W -> Γ_f and (q_X,q_Z) : W -> Γ_{g∘f} are proper birational; (q_Y,q_Z) : W -> Γ_g is proper, surjective, generically finite of degree e(f).
hypotheses: X, Y, Z projective varieties of the same dimension

targets.name: RationalMap.graph_normalization / RationalMap.graph_baseChange
targets.statement: Normalization: for ν : X̃ -> X and f̃ = ν^{-1}∘f∘ν, ν×ν maps Γ_{f̃} properly and birationally onto Γ_f, and (f^n)~ = f̃^n. Field extension: (Γ_f)_{K'} is the scheme-theoretic image of γ_f ×_K K'; for X, Y geometrically integral, f_{K'} is dominant, e(f_{K'}) = e(f), (g∘f)_{K'} = g_{K'}∘f_{K'}, Γ_{f_{K'}} = (Γ_f)_{K'}. The degree equality is proved by cases: if dim X = dim Y, a basis of K(X) over f^*K(Y) of e(f) ≥ 1 elements stays a basis after ⊗_K K' and localization; if dim X > dim Y, K(X) is infinite-dimensional over f^*K(Y), no finite basis is used, and invariance of dimension gives e(f_{K'}) = 0 = e(f).
hypotheses: X projective variety, f dominant self-map for the normalization part
X, Y geometrically integral for the statements on f_{K'}
no equal-dimension hypothesis for e(f_{K'}) = e(f): the case dim X > dim Y is the junk value 0 on both sides

locator.where: Lemma 26.16 (tag 081I), line 2198; truong2020 §6.3, line 1529

targets.name: realIntersectionForm
targets.statement: The symmetric R-multilinear extension of (L_1,…,L_r) ↦ (L_1⋯L_r)_X to Pic(X) ⊗ R, with linear pullback; projection formula and field-extension invariance extend. A real class ω = Σ t_i L_i (real t_i of any sign) is nef if (ω·C) = Σ t_i (L_i·C) ≥ 0 for every integral closed curve C ⊆ X, equivalently if its image in N^1(X/K) (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometryPartII §1.1) lies in the nef cone Nef(X/K) (its §1.5); every class of Nef(X/K) comes from a nef real class; a real polarization is a nef real class with (ω^d) > 0.
hypotheses: X proper over K of dimension ≤ r

targets.name: isNef_iff_intersectionNumber_nonneg / isNef_baseChange_iff
targets.statement: Nefness is imported from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometryPartII §1.5 over the base Spec K (nonnegative degree on every integral curve of a proper K-scheme; sums, positive multiples, pullback, preservation under field extension), with ample implies nef from its §1.7. Nef real classes are those of §2.3 (nonnegative degree on every integral curve, i.e. nef image in N^1(X/K)); they can be strictly more than the positive combinations of nef line bundles. This section proves: L is nef iff (L·C) ≥ 0 for every integral closed curve, with the numerical intersection (the coefficient of n in χ(C, nL) is the degree χ(C,L) − χ(C,O_C)); on a projective variety this is ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII §0.1's nefness; big and nef pulls back to big and nef along generically finite surjective maps of equal dimension with ((p^*L)^d) = deg(p)(L^d); for every projective K-scheme, L nef iff L_{K'} nef (forward direction imported, converse through §2.1 and field-extension compatibility); nefness passes to W of §2.4; pullbacks of nef real classes along K-morphisms of proper K-schemes are nef, and real polarizations pull back along generically finite surjective maps of equal dimension with ((p^*ω)^d) = deg(p)(ω^d); ample approximation: on a proper K-scheme with an ample H, for nef real classes ω_j = Σ_{i=1}^n t_{ji} L_i, an integer m ≥ 1 with mH ± L_i ample, every rational δ > 0 and rationals t'_{ji} with |t'_{ji} - t_{ji}| ≤ δ/(2mn), Σ_i t'_{ji} L_i + δH = N^{-1}A_j with N ≥ 1 and A_j ample line bundles; hence an inequality P ≤ Q between polynomials in intersection numbers, homogeneous of the same degree in each class on both sides, that holds for ample line bundles holds for all nef real classes.
hypotheses: X projective (for the field-extension item) or proper over K
X with an ample line bundle H for the ample approximation

locator.where: §2.2, lines 274-287 (nef classes over an arbitrary field); the definition is AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometryPartII §1.5

targets.name: projectiveSpace_rationalMap_forms
targets.statement: Forms F_0..F_d of a common degree, not all zero, define a unique K-rational map of P^d; every K-rational map of P^d is given by forms without common factor, unique up to a scalar, of degree deg f, with domain the complement of V(F) (codimension ≥ 2). Composition: for f = [F] dominant and g = [G] any rational map (reduced forms), G(F) is not identically zero, g∘f = [G(F)/gcd], deg(g∘f) ≤ deg f·deg g, with equality if f or g is a morphism. Iterates of morphisms: a morphism of degree a ≥ 1 is finite, surjective and dominant, with iterates of degree a^n; a morphism of degree 0 is constant, not dominant, and its iterates are taken in the composition of morphisms (RationalMap.compHom): f^0 = id, f^n = f for n ≥ 1, so deg(f^n) = (deg f)^n with 0^0 = 1.
